One day, your child won’t be this little anymore. And you might just wish you could have one more of these quiet moments, holding their little feet in your hands. 🤍 But did you know there’s a Reflexology technique you can learn to make these moments even more meaningful? Let me show you the Lung Reflex. 👣 In Foot Reflexology, the Lung Reflex is found across the ball of each foot, just beneath the toes. It’s traditionally associated with the lungs and chest, and working this area with gentle, rhythmic movements can be a lovely addition to a relaxing evening routine. Here’s how to try it: 🤍 Hold your child’s foot comfortably in your hands. 🤍 Using the soft pad of your thumb, gently walk across the ball of the foot, applying light, comfortable pressure. 🤍 Keep your movements slow and unhurried, following your child’s response. 🤍 Repeat on the other foot if they’d like you to. No rushing. No pressure. Just a few precious minutes together. As a Clinical Reflexologist practising since 2008, I want more mums to feel confident using simple Foot Reflexology techniques with their children. Because sometimes the smallest rituals become the moments we remember most. Want to learn more? 🤍 I’ve created a FREE Evening Edit with three simple bedtime rituals you can try with your child. ✨ Find your free guide through the LINK IN MY BIO. The key to a strong and stable structure lies beneath the surface. Let’s dig into the fascinating world of footings! 🔍 🌐 Footing Fundamentals: Footing is the unsung hero of construction, responsible for transferring the weight of a building to the solid ground below. It’s a game-changer! But how do you choose the right type of footing? 🤔 ✅ Factors to Consider: 1️⃣ Depth of Safe-Bearing Strata 2️⃣ Soil Type & Condition 3️⃣ Superstructure’s Needs 🏠 Isolated Footing: When you’ve got single columns standing solo, isolated footings are your go-to choice. These footings ensure stability, prevent sinking, and keep things safe and sound. 💰 Cost-Effective Choice: Isolated footings are often the budget-friendly option, especially when the ground’s properties remain consistent. Now, let’s talk types of isolated footings: 1️⃣ Pad Footing: Versatile in shape, efficient, but watch out for lateral forces! What’s your preference – circular, rectangular, or square? 2️⃣ Sloped Footing: Less concrete, less reinforcement, and a sleek 45-degree slope. It’s all about maintaining that perfect angle! 📐 3️⃣ Stepped Footing: A classic approach for residential buildings, although it’s become less common in recent years. 🏘️ 4️⃣ Combined Footing: When space is tight, and individual footings won’t cut it, we combine forces! 💪 What’s your experience with footings?
